downstream_workflows.canonical_definition: Downstream workflows are workflows that happen after the parent workflow and consume, continue, execute, monitor, or act upon the output, result, decision, object, document, or final state produced by the parent workflow.
downstream_workflows.purpose: They define what is outside and after the parent workflow, while explaining what the parent workflow enables or hands off to.
downstream_workflows.relationship_rule: A workflow is downstream when it receives an output from the parent workflow and starts, continues, or becomes possible because the parent workflow has reached its end state.
what_it_is_not: It is not an internal completion step of the parent workflow.
It is not an upstream workflow that produces the initial trigger.
It is not adjacent if it clearly depends on the parent workflow's final output.
It should not be merged into the parent workflow unless the selected analysis scope explicitly includes post-completion execution or follow-up.

examples.name: post-discharge home care workflow
examples.relationship_to_parent: Starts after the hospital discharge workflow produces a discharge plan and care instructions.
examples.input_received_from_parent: Discharge plan and patient handoff information.

examples.name: invoice payment workflow
examples.relationship_to_parent: Starts after the invoice approval workflow approves the invoice.
